title: Keep resolved ESM loaders as file URLs, never convert to filesystem paths
context: Node.js `--import` flag requires a URL argument. The code was converting `import.meta.resolve('tsx')` to a filesystem path via `fileURLToPath()`, causing Node to reject it on Windows with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME, breaking task verification. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Pass the resolved loader directly as a file URL to `--import`, with defensive handling for non-URL-formatted resolves. Added test assertion to enforce that verification launcher always provides file URLs to `--import`.
consequences: Task verification now works on Windows and all platforms
Contribution cards show verification checks instead of failing silently
Native format preservation (URL) is simpler than bidirectional path/URL conversion
Future changes to the loader resolution are protected by the test assertion
alternatives_rejected: Work around it at Node invocation level instead of fixing at source
Try to normalize Windows paths differently (won't work—Node requires URL format)
Skip test assertion to avoid 'overspecification' (regression risk)
